solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of poem on spiteful woman facing a calamity

blocks.note: a cat is a catty, spiteful woman
taken as written
a strophe is a stanza or section of a poem

explanation.surface: A poet writes some verse about a nasty woman who is heading for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the poem part after the woman; 'facing a' sets the A beside her, so the pieces read woman, A, poem part. The definition carries its article: 'a calamity' is a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a sudden disaster, the same thing as a calamity.

clue.text: Unfriendly measures causing loss of confidence

blocks.note: a cold manner is unfriendly
feet are units of length, or metrical measures in verse

explanation.surface: Hostile policies make people lose their nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cold feet is the idiom for losing your nerve just before doing something.

clue.text: Row over warning device becoming more unpleasant

indicators.note: one thing laid over another covers it, so the first word's letters enclose the second's

blocks.note: a tier is a row of seats
a car horn warns other road users

explanation.surface: An argument about a car alarm gets nastier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line of seats, and 'over' wraps it around the warning device.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorny means prickly or troublesome, so thornier is a comparative meaning more awkward and unpleasant.

clue.text: Quick to discard piece of pie when out of sorts

indicators.note: to discard something is to throw it away, so a letter is removed from the word
a piece of a word here is just its opening letter

blocks.note: speedy means quick
the first letter of pie

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell is quick to leave a slice of pie uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEEDY drops its P to leave SEEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling seedy is a British informal way of being slightly unwell or under the weather.

clue.text: Soldiers present in keep

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
to serve is to present, as with food or a writ

explanation.surface: Troops on duty inside a castle's keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a castle tower but is a verb: to keep back, to hold in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to hold it back for later, which is what keeping it means.

clue.text: Stop parking right outside flat

indicators.note: letters placed outside another word surround it on both sides

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Rt is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
a flat surface is even

explanation.surface: An order to stop leaving cars directly outside an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' pretends to be a home but means level, and 'right' here is its two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening.

clue.text: Daughter behind door spellbound

indicators.note: behind places the family member's letter after the doorway word, at the back

blocks.note: a door is an entrance
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl standing behind a door is enthralled by what she hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the daughter's letter after the doorway word.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced means held in a trance, completely captivated, just as spellbound is.

clue.text: Blue sky at first today

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the first letter of sky
AD, anno domini, marks the present era, so it stands for today

explanation.surface: A weather note: the sky is blue early today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like the sky's colour but means unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is an idiom for being sad or low in spirits.

clue.text: Be absorbed in last of games at home with relatives

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: the last letter of games
someone at home is in
your kin are your relatives

explanation.surface: Getting lost in the final rounds of a game while staying in with family.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is S, then IN, then KIN, giving SINK IN.
explanation.definitionFit: When news sinks in, it is gradually understood, soaking into the mind as liquid is absorbed.

clue.text: Fearless lawyer going after gang? Just the opposite

indicators.text: going after gang? Just the opposite
indicators.note: going after would put the lawyer second; just the opposite flips that order so the lawyer leads

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
a ring is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: A brave prosecutor chases down a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after gang' would put the lawyer second; 'Just the opposite' reverses that instruction, so the lawyer comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring describes someone bold and willing to take risks, so unafraid.

clue.text: Relaxed game of cards with a couple from Seoul

indicators.note: a couple from a word means its first two letters

blocks.note: loo is an old trick-taking card game
the first two letters of Seoul

explanation.surface: A laid-back card game played with a pair of people from Korea.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a card game as well as British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means slack or not tight, which is relaxed.

clue.text: Amiable Frenchman taken aback by bribe

indicators.note: taken aback, read literally, means carried backwards, so the name runs right to left

blocks.note: a sweet person is kind and amiable
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A friendly Frenchman is startled at being offered a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as surprised, but works literally: RENE backwards gives ENER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an informal word for an inducement or bribe that makes a deal more attractive.

clue.text: Not emotionally involved with anyone like Frank

blocks.note: to fancy something is to like it
frank speech is free and open

explanation.surface: Someone like Frank who has no romantic attachments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but the capital is only for the surface: it means outspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free means without romantic ties, as in the phrase footloose and fancy-free.

clue.text: Clip the wings of most important foreigner

indicators.note: clipping a bird's wings trims both sides, so the outer letters are cut off

blocks.note: the salient points are the most important ones

explanation.surface: An instruction to curb the power of the chief outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: SALIENT loses its first and last letters to give ALIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a person from another country, an old legal term for a foreign national.

clue.text: Do without earl appealing

blocks.note: ex means without, as in shares sold ex dividend
E is an abbreviation for earl
something cute is appealing

explanation.surface: An appealing nobleman can be done without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do without' reads as a phrase, but 'Do' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a plan is to carry it out or perform it, which is to do it.

clue.text: Dour and nervous crossing north-eastern plain

indicators.note: a nervous person is jittery and unsettled, so these letters will not stay put
crossing means straddling something, so these letters span around the inserted abbreviation

blocks.note: the letters of dour and, rearranged
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A grim, anxious traveller crosses a flat stretch of the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a noun for flat land, but it is the adjective meaning undecorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means without decoration, which is a sense of plain.

clue.text: The principal function of diplomacy

indicators.note: the principal part of a word is its leading letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the
to function is to act or operate

explanation.surface: A statement of what diplomacy is mainly for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The principal function' reads as one phrase, but only T comes from 'The', with ACT for function.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is skill in handling people sensitively, which is the essence of diplomacy.

clue.text: Supplication to curb mythical god's excess

indicators.note: to curb something is to hold it in check, so one word restrains another inside it

blocks.note: a plea is a supplication or earnest request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A prayer asking a deity to restrain his overindulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on god's is surface glue, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an overabundance, more than is needed, so an excess.

clue.text: Bearing the cost of conveyance

blocks.note: first meaning: the way a person holds their body, posture
second meaning: the charge for transporting goods

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about paying for transport; 'Bearing' is a separate meaning, a person's posture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's deportment and the fee charged for transporting goods, as in carriage paid.

clue.text: Dress rehearsal's opening feeds gossip

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
something that feeds goes into a mouth, so this letter is put inside the other word

blocks.note: gab is idle chatter or gossip
the first letter of rehearsal

explanation.surface: Backstage chatter at the start of a dress rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress rehearsal' reads as a theatre phrase, but 'Dress' alone is the definition. R goes inside GAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, often distinctive, so it is a synonym of dress as a noun.

clue.text: Country bumpkin's original letter turned up in support of the Spanish soldier

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is the one it starts with
in a down answer, turning something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first letter of bumpkin
el is Spanish for the
a GI is an American soldier
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A rustic's first letter, an envelope, arrives for a Spanish soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'in support of' puts the reversed letter UM beneath EL and GI, holding them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgium is a country in western Europe.

clue.text: Dad with hint of listlessness stops using lead frying pan

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just a trace of it, its first letter
using something means working it over, so these letters are worked into a new order
a stopper sits inside a bottle's neck, so this letter plugs the inside of the other word

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father
the letters of lead, rearranged
the first letter of listlessness

explanation.surface: A lethargic father gives up cooking with a pan made of lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the metal, but it is only letters to rearrange; 'stops' means the hint letter plugs them.
explanation.definitionFit: A padella is the Italian word for a frying pan, also used in English for a shallow pan-shaped dish.

clue.text: Mercurial prince leaves during middle of song

indicators.note: something that happens during an event is inside its span, so one piece sits within another
middle of takes the central letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: Pr is an abbreviation for prince
the middle two letters of song
tea comes as leaves, so leaves can stand for tea

explanation.surface: A moody prince walks out in the middle of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, a prince departing, but it is a noun: the leaves you brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Protean, from the shape-changing sea god Proteus, means changeable, as does mercurial.

clue.text: Drug like heroin found in plant nutrient

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
as means like, in the manner of
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A heroin-like drug discovered in a fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound widely used as a fertiliser, feeding plants.

clue.text: Tabulated numerical facts about university's standing

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word's letters go around the next

blocks.note: stats is short for statistics, numbers often set out in tables
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: League tables of figures shape a university's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after university stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is a person's or body's rank or position in society, its standing.

clue.text: Excel when no longer in party

blocks.note: something no longer in is out
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone shines once they have left the political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excel' looks like the spreadsheet but is the verb to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to do better than them, to excel or surpass.

clue.text: Be responsible for talker of nonsense about love

indicators.note: nonsense is jumbled sense, so these words come out scrambled
about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go around the symbol for zero

blocks.note: the letters of talker of, rearranged
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Taking charge of someone who talks rubbish about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside the rearranged TALKEROF, after its first letter, to give LOOK AFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after something is the phrasal verb for taking care of it, being in charge of it.

clue.text: American gin served up separately

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending something up makes it read from the bottom

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for American
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: A bartender in the States pours gin into separate glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the spirit but is the hunter's snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separately, away from each other.

clue.text: Mindful of taint Eve developed over time

indicators.note: something developed has been reworked and changed, so these letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to rearrange
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Eve's guilt developed as time went by, to her own awareness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over time' adds the T to the letters of taint Eve before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being attentive means paying close attention, so heedful or mindful.

clue.text: Peculiar charm of article on artist receiving award

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
an RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An odd appeal surrounds a painter who has just won a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' looks like strange, but here means particular to one thing, characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive, characteristic quality or atmosphere surrounding something, its special allure.

clue.text: Evident in anarchism associated with that fellow

indicators.note: evident in a word means visible within its letters

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively inside anarchism

explanation.surface: A man known for his link to anarchist politics.
explanation.definitionFit: His is the possessive pronoun for a man, meaning belonging to that fellow.

clue.text: Devils meeting resistance in art gallery show

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: demons are devils
the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Evil spirits clash with protesters at an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' at the end looks like an art show, but it is the verb to prove.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate something is to show it clearly or prove it.
